subject: Physics
title: Kinetic Theory
summary: A gas is a huge number of tiny molecules in random motion. Their collisions with the walls produce pressure: P = ⅓ρv²_rms.
Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules: average translational KE per molecule = (3/2)kT, independent of the gas.
Equipartition: every degree of freedom gets ½kT per molecule. Counting degrees of freedom gives Cv, Cp and γ of monoatomic, diatomic and polyatomic gases.
Mean free path — the average distance between collisions — is λ = kT/(√2 π d² P): it grows as the gas gets hotter or thinner.

formulas.name: Ideal gas equation
formulas.formula: PV = nRT = N k T;  R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹,  k = R/Nₐ = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K
formulas.when: Any problem connecting P, V, T and amount of gas.
formulas.note: Use kelvin, and SI units for P and V (1 L = 10⁻³ m³).

formulas.name: Pressure of an ideal gas
formulas.formula: P = ⅓ (N m/V) v²_rms = ⅓ ρ v²_rms

formulas.name: Kinetic energy and temperature
formulas.formula: average translational KE per molecule = (3/2) k T;   per mole = (3/2) R T
formulas.note: It depends only on T — every gas at the same T has the same average translational KE.

formulas.name: RMS speed
formulas.mistake: M in kg/mol (0.032 for O₂), not g/mol.

formulas.name: Degrees of freedom
formulas.formula: monoatomic f = 3;  diatomic f = 5 (rigid) or 7 (with vibration);  non-linear polyatomic f = 6 (rigid)

formulas.name: Law of equipartition
formulas.formula: energy per degree of freedom = ½ k T per molecule;  U = (f/2) n R T

formulas.name: Specific heats from f
formulas.when: Finding γ and molar heat capacities.

formulas.name: Mean free path
formulas.formula: λ = k T / (√2 π d² P) = 1/(√2 n π d²)
formulas.note: λ ∝ T/P — doubling pressure halves λ.

formulas.name: Avogadro's number
formulas.formula: Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹;  molar volume at STP ≈ 22.4 L

formulas.name: Gas laws (special cases)
formulas.formula: Boyle: PV = const (T fixed);  Charles: V/T = const (P fixed);  Gay-Lussac: P/T = const (V fixed);  Dalton: P = P₁ + P₂ + …

formulas.name: Pressure in a rotating gas (isothermal)
formulas.formula: dP/dr = ρω²r with ρ = PM/RT  ⇒  P(r) = P_axis · e^(Mω²r²/2RT);  tube of length l rotated about end A: P_B = P_A e^(Mω²l²/2RT)
formulas.when: Closed tube of gas spun about an axis at the same temperature — pressure is higher at the far end.
formulas.note: M = molar mass (kg/mol). For an incompressible liquid instead: P = P_axis + ½ρω²r².

topics.title: Assumptions of kinetic theory
topics.explain: Molecules are point-like, move randomly, collide elastically with each other and the walls, exert no force except during collisions, and the time of a collision is negligible. Real gases follow this at low pressure and high temperature.

topics.title: Molecular nature of matter
topics.explain: Matter is made of atoms and molecules (Dalton's atomic theory). Avogadro's hypothesis: equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

topics.title: Meaning of temperature
topics.explain: Temperature is proportional to the average translational KE of molecules. At absolute zero this motion (classically) stops.

topics.title: Degrees of freedom in detail
topics.explain: A monoatomic gas (He, Ar) has 3 translational. A diatomic gas (O₂, N₂) adds 2 rotational = 5; at high temperature vibration adds 2 more = 7. A non-linear molecule (H₂O, CH₄) has 3 translational + 3 rotational = 6.

topics.title: Specific heat of solids
topics.explain: By equipartition each atom of a solid has 6 quadratic terms (3 KE + 3 PE), giving molar heat capacity ≈ 3R (Dulong–Petit law), true at high temperature.

topics.title: Mean free path and diffusion
topics.explain: Molecules travel fast (~500 m/s) but collide so often that a smell takes a long time to spread across a room. λ increases at low pressure — the basis of vacuum technology.

topics.title: Real vs ideal gas
topics.explain: Real gases deviate because molecules have finite size and attract each other — most at high pressure and low temperature.

ratta: Cv = fR/2, Cp = Cv + R, γ = 1 + 2/f.
